html:
SMTO-ART-0015 — This saved file has been deleted or set aside

GUID: ad27d5f9-4f07-4c44-bc27-32a2b8b73a1c
Slug: artifact-deleted
Domain: ART · Subsystem: art

What happened

  • SMTO no longer gives out this file. It was deleted, or SMTO set it aside because its stored copy was missing or damaged.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Close the file, then open Artifacts from this run again so the list is up to date. You may be using an older link to a copy that has since been replaced or removed.
  2. Look for the same file name with a Download link in that list and use that copy. When a Task saves a file again, SMTO keeps the newer copy available even if an older one was set aside.
  3. If no copy is available and the original file still exists, ask SMTO in a new message to save it again. A fresh save makes a new checked copy; deleted copies can't be brought back.

What success looks like

  • You can download the file from the current Artifacts from this run list.

If it still fails

  • If files keep being set aside, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO; it can point to a storage problem on the server. Don't reuse old file links from earlier messages.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Opening the artifact stream was refused because its registry status is not available: it was deleted by retention or purge, or quarantined after a missing or integrity-failed blob.

What this means

  • Artifact stream opening finds the registry status other than available, including deleted or quarantined. Artifact publication and presentation remain separate from the command that produced a file. Only an explicit pre-dispatch rejection proves that new command did not run; diagnostics do not collect, transfer, quarantine or delete files.

Why this can happen

  • Artifact stream opening finds the registry status other than available, including deleted or quarantined.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect exact registry status and retained source before assuming deletion and quarantine mean the same thing.

How to fix it

  • Check registered_artifacts.status and the run's artifact events for the artifact ID; quarantine comes from an open_stream integrity failure, maintenance missing-file detection or a tampered predecessor version. Select the latest available version from the run's artifact list, or re-collect from the source if it still exists; do not set the status back to available by hand.
  • Refresh the owning run’s artifact list. Recollect from the authoritative source if that source still exists.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported available verified artifact is selected or deliberately recollected from an existing authoritative source.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Artifact publication and presentation remain separate from the command that produced a file. Only an explicit pre-dispatch rejection proves that new command did not run; diagnostics do not collect, transfer, quarantine or delete files.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
